ground_truth.threatName: Unauthorized Access to Knowledge Base S3 Bucket

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could exploit misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or leaked AWS credentials to access sensitive documents in the S3 bucket.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker obtains AWS credentials from a public code repository or through a compromised system and uses them to download sensitive documents from the S3 bucket.

recommendations.description: Implement strict S3 bucket access controls
recommendations.implementationDetails: Ensure S3 bucket has block public access enabled, uses AWS KMS encryption, and enforces SSL. Implement least privilege IAM policies for Lambda function access.

recommendations.description: Enable S3 bucket logging and monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable CloudTrail and CloudWatch logging for S3 bucket access. Set up alerts for unauthorized access attempts and suspicious patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code already implements S3 bucket encryption and blocks public access. Consider adding server access logging and implementing additional CloudWatch alarms for monitoring access patterns.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Storing authentication tokens in browser localStorage or sessionStorage makes them vulnerable to XSS attacks and malicious browser extensions.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker exploits an XSS vulnerability to inject JavaScript that extracts authentication tokens from localStorage and sends them to a malicious server.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Store tokens in HTTP-only cookies with secure and same-site attributes. Implement proper token rotation and revocation mechanisms.
Use short-lived access tokens, implement proper refresh token rotation, and revoke refresh tokens on sign-out or security events.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Cognito provides built-in token management capabilities. Ensure proper implementation of token handling in the Next.js application.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: The AI model might include PII in its responses or store sensitive information in chat history, leading to potential privacy violations.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A user asks questions that prompt the AI to reveal PII from the knowledge base or previous conversations.

recommendations.description: Implement AI guardrails and PII detection
recommendations.implementationDetails: Use Bedrock guardrails to prevent PII exposure. Implement automated PII detection and redaction in both inputs and outputs.
Set up automated processes to detect and purge PII from chat history and vector database regularly.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code includes PII redaction feature flag. Ensure proper implementation of Bedrock guardrails and regular PII cleanup processes.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could attempt to inject malicious code through chat inputs or file uploads that could be executed in the application environment.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker crafts special input that exploits input validation vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the Fargate container.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement comprehensive input validation and sanitization for all user inputs. Use parameterized queries and escape special characters.
Apply security hardening to Fargate containers and Lambda functions. Implement least privilege permissions and runtime protection.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS WAF rules to filter malicious inputs. Consider implementing AWS GuardDuty for additional threat detection.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Weaknesses in authentication implementation could allow attackers to bypass authentication or hijack sessions.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker intercepts authorization codes or exploits missing PKCE implementation to gain unauthorized access.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement PKCE, enforce TLS 1.2+, use secure client secret handling, and implement proper scope restrictions.
Implement WAF rules to protect authentication endpoints from abuse and implement rate limiting.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code includes WAF and Cognito configuration. Ensure proper implementation of PKCE and secure token handling.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers could craft malicious inputs that exploit vector database query vulnerabilities to access or manipulate data.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker injects malicious parameters into vector similarity search queries to extract unauthorized data.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement proper input validation for vector queries, use parameterized queries, and implement least privilege access.
Implement logging and monitoring for vector database queries. Set up alerts for suspicious patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: OpenSearch Serverless provides built-in security features. Ensure proper implementation of access policies and encryption.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Overly permissive security groups or improperly configured VPC endpoints could allow unauthorized network access.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker exploits overly permissive security group rules to access internal services directly.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Implement least privilege security groups, proper subnet segmentation, and secure VPC endpoint configuration.
Implement VPC Flow Logs and network monitoring. Set up alerts for suspicious traffic patterns.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: The CDK code implements security groups and VPC endpoints. Ensure proper configuration and regular security reviews.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Without proper logging and monitoring, attackers could perform malicious activities without detection.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker gains access to the system and exfiltrates data, but the activity goes unnoticed due to insufficient logging.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable CloudTrail and CloudWatch logging for all AWS services. Implement centralized log collection and analysis.
Set up GuardDuty for threat detection. Implement automated alerts for security events.

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Enable AWS Config for resource configuration monitoring. Consider implementing AWS Security Hub for centralized security management.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
AWS AI-Powered Assistant Architecture Diagram Generator

This script generates an architecture diagram for an AI-powered assistant
designed to provide rapid, accurate responses to queries about internal data.
The architecture leverages various AWS services, particularly Amazon Bedrock,
to create a secure, efficient, and intelligent solution.
"""

# Import the diagrams package
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge, Node

# Custom icons for users
from diagrams.onprem.client import Users

# Storage related imports
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# Compute related imports
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda, ECS, Fargate

# Network related imports
from diagrams.aws.network import VPC, ElbApplicationLoadBalancer, Endpoint

# Security related imports
from diagrams.aws.security import Cognito, WAF

# Database related imports
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb
from diagrams.aws.analytics import AmazonOpensearchService

# Integration related imports
from diagrams.aws.integration import Eventbridge

# Machine Learning related imports
from diagrams.aws.ml import Bedrock

# Define diagram attributes
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "30",
    "fontcolor": "#333333",
    "bgcolor": "#FFFFFF",
    "rankdir": "LR",  # Changed from TB to LR for horizontal layout
    "splines": "curved",  # Changed from ortho to curved for flexible arrows
    "nodesep": "0.8",
    "ranksep": "1.0",
    "pad": "1.0"
}

# Define node attributes
node_attr = {
    "fontsize": "12",
    "fontcolor": "#333333",
    "shape": "box",
    "style": "rounded",
    "fixedsize": "true",
    "width": "1.6",
    "height": "1.6"
}

# Define edge attributes
edge_attr = {
    "fontsize": "10",
    "fontcolor": "#555555"
}

# Create the diagram
with Diagram(
    name="AWS AI-Powered Assistant Architecture",
    filename="aws_ai_assistant_architecture",
    outformat="png",
    show=False,
    direction="LR",  # Changed from TB to LR for horizontal layout
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    node_attr=node_attr,
    edge_attr=edge_attr
) as diag:
    
    # Define edge styles
    data_flow = Edge(color="#2171B5", style="solid", label="Data Flow")
    event_trigger = Edge(color="#238B45", style="dashed", label="Event Trigger")
    auth_flow = Edge(color="#CB181D", style="solid", label="Auth Flow")
    service_connection = Edge(color="#6A51A3", style="dotted", label="Service Connection")
    
    # Define user flow styles
    data_prep_flow = Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold")
    app_user_flow = Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold")
    
    # Create user icons on the left side
    with Cluster("Users", graph_attr={"color": "transparent"}):
        cloud_admins = Users("Cloud Admins")
        chatbot_users = Users("Chatbot Users")
    
    # Main architecture with two main sections
    
    # Data Preparation Pipeline (Step 1) - Top section with purple border
    with Cluster("Knowledge base data pipeline stack", graph_attr={"style": "dashed", "color": "#C71585", "penwidth": "2.0"}):
        s3 = S3("Amazon S3\n(with\nknowledge\nbase)")
        s3_event = Eventbridge("Amazon S3\nevent trigger\n(upload or\nedit objects)")
        lambda_processor = Lambda("AWS Lambda\n(parse data\nand convert\nto\nembeddings\nvector db)")
        titan_embedding = Bedrock("Amazon Bedrock\n(Titan Embedding Model)")
        
        # Numbers will be added directly to the edges
    
    # Application Deployment (Step 2) - Bottom section with green border
    with Cluster("Chatbot application stack", graph_attr={"style": "dashed", "color": "#228B22", "penwidth": "2.0"}):
        # Security services outside VPC
        cognito = Cognito("Amazon\nCognito\n(Auth)")
        waf = WAF("AWS WAF\n(Managed\nfirewall rules)")
        
        # VPC for Application Deployment
        with Cluster("VPC", graph_attr={"color": "#228B22"}):
            # Public subnet
            with Cluster("Public subnet", graph_attr={"bgcolor": "#E0FFE0"}):
                alb = ElbApplicationLoadBalancer("Application\nLoad Balancer")
            
            # Private subnet for application
            with Cluster("Private subnet", graph_attr={"bgcolor": "#E0F0FF"}):
                # ECS Fargate cluster
                with Cluster("ECS Cluster", graph_attr={"color": "#FF9900"}):
                    web_app = ECS("Next.JS Web Application\n(Docker)")
                    fargate = Fargate("Fargate")
                    web_app - fargate
                
                # Lambda Web Adapter
                lambda_web_adapter = Lambda("AWS Lambda Web Adapter (python)")
        
        # Backend AWS Services section
        with Cluster("Backend AWS Services", graph_attr={"bgcolor": "#FFF0E0"}):
            # VPC Endpoints
            with Cluster("VPC Service Endpoints", graph_attr={"color": "#777777"}):
                bedrock_endpoint = Endpoint("Bedrock Endpoint")
                opensearch_endpoint = Endpoint("OpenSearch Endpoint")
                dynamodb_endpoint = Endpoint("DynamoDB Endpoint")
            
            # Backend Services
            opensearch = AmazonOpensearchService("Amazon OpenSearch\nServerless\n(Vector Database)")
            bedrock_guardrail = Bedrock("Amazon Bedrock\nGuardrail\n(Responsible AI\nChecks & PII\nRedact)")
            claude_model = Bedrock("Amazon Bedrock\n(Anthropic\nClaude Model)")
            dynamodb = Dynamodb("Amazon\nDynamoDB\n(Chat History)")
            
            # Numbers will be added directly to the edges
    
    # Define the connections for Data Preparation Pipeline with "Step-1: Data Preparation" label
    cloud_admins >> Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold", label="Step-1: Data Preparation") >> s3
    s3 >> Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold", label="1") >> s3_event
    s3_event >> Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold", label="2") >> lambda_processor
    lambda_processor >> Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold", label="3") >> titan_embedding
    lambda_processor >> Edge(color="#C71585", style="bold", label="4") >> opensearch
    
    # Define the connections for Application Deployment (Step 2) by Cloud Admins - pointing to the whole stack
    cloud_admins >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="Step-2: Application Deployment") >> cognito
    
    # Define the connections for User Authentication and Request Handling by Chatbot Users
    chatbot_users >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="Application Access") >> cognito
    cognito >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="1") >> waf
    waf >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="2") >> alb
    alb >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="3") >> web_app
    # Add arrow from ALB back to Chatbot Users (response direction)
    alb >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="Response") >> chatbot_users
    
    # Define the connections for Application Processing
    web_app >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="4") >> lambda_web_adapter
    
    # Define the connections for Backend Processing - VPC endpoints called from ECS cluster
    web_app >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="5") >> bedrock_endpoint
    
    # Connect to backend services
    # Removed arrow from bedrock_endpoint to opensearch
    opensearch_endpoint >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="OpenSearch Connection") >> opensearch
    bedrock_endpoint >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="6") >> bedrock_guardrail
    bedrock_guardrail >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="7") >> claude_model
    claude_model >> Edge(color="#228B22", style="bold", label="8") >> lambda_web_adapter
    
    # Connect DynamoDB endpoint to DynamoDB
    dynamodb_endpoint >> app_user_flow >> dynamodb

    # Legend removed as requested

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("AWS AI-Powered Assistant Architecture diagram generated successfully.")
    print("Output file: aws_ai_assistant_architecture.png")
